feedback: All checks pass. Function set: exactly the five environment-declared propositions (blocker_moved, has_door_key, door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost); no undeclared extras, none missing, and the RM-unused declared predicates (has_door_key, door_open, target_picked_up, key_lost) are correctly present. blocker_moved: scans for the unique door by type and checks the cell at (x-1, y) — the documented start-side front cell (dx-1, dy) where the ball spawns; 'x > 0' is a safe guard (the shared-wall door always has dx >= 1, and out-of-bounds is avoided by short-circuiting). It returns True when the ball is picked up (cell empty on grid) or dropped elsewhere, and False again when the ball is dropped back on that cell — matching the non-latch condition reading exactly. has_door_key, door_open, and target_picked_up match the documented expressions verbatim: key color matched against the door's color via a guarded grid scan, door openness read from is_open, and the target box matched through env.mission (no hard-coded color). key_lost: correct event semantics — reads env.episode_memory['previous_valuation'] read-only, requires prev has_door_key true, key not carried now, and door not open now; true only on the drop step, false otherwise, and false at step one since the initial valuation is all-false. The inline recomputation of K and D is equivalent to referencing the other predicates. Safety: no imports, no actions, no mutations of env or episode_memory, only documented API attributes used, every cell/carrying access guarded with 'is not None' before attribute reads, returns are proper booleans (key_lost normalized with bool()), and all five functions are syntactically valid, executable Python taking only env.
